Scope_Note_SN: Fixed-wing aircraft facility where flights take off, land, and passengers connect between legs. AMS (Amsterdam Schiphol) is KLM's home hub; the other nine airports in this network are spokes.
The passenger-facing building at an airport handling check-in, security, boarding, and arrivals processing.
Airport facility handling belly cargo and freight loading/unloading, kept separate from passenger flow.
Facility coordinating aircraft turnaround: baggage handling, catering, fueling, and pushback services on the ramp.
Airport counter where connecting passengers get rebooking help, boarding passes, and MCT (minimum connecting time) guidance.
Automated terminal for passenger check-in and self-service bag drop, reducing counter queue time.
An airport role: the carrier's central connecting point where most routes originate or terminate. AMS is KLM's sole hub airport.
An airport role: a point-to-point destination served from the hub, without its own onward connecting bank.
An airport role: a spoke airport that itself serves as a long-haul gateway for onward intercontinental connections (e.g. JFK, SIN, HND, GRU).
The commercial entity operating a flight and holding responsibility for its schedule, crew, and passenger service.
The primary carrier operating a flight under its own brand and flight numbers — KLM for the flights in this network.
A partner airline (e.g. Delta on the transatlantic joint venture) that markets or operates a flight jointly with the mainline carrier.
Pilots and cabin crew rostered to operate a flight, employed by or contracted to an airline.
A scheduled origin-destination pair an airline operates, e.g. AMS-JFK, independent of any specific day's flight instance.
A physical aircraft, identified by its tail number, that operates flights along an assigned route rotation.
Twin-aisle aircraft used on long-haul intercontinental routes — B777-300ER, B787-9/10, A330-300 in this fleet.
Single-aisle aircraft used on medium-haul European routes — the A321neo family in this fleet.
Single-aisle aircraft used on short intra-European hops — the B737-800 family in this fleet.
Smaller single-aisle jets used on thinner short-haul routes — the E195-E2 family in this fleet.
A single scheduled operating instance of a route on a specific day, carrying passengers under a connection-time SLA — the at-risk/flow entity tracked for disruption.
The binding of a specific aircraft tail number to a flight leg within its daily rotation.
A real-time operational signal — a fault, delay, or position update — emitted by an airport or aircraft that operations control monitors.
An aircraft maintenance defect logged against the tech log, potentially grounding or delaying the aircraft.
An unexpected spike in passenger or connecting-bag volume at a terminal beyond planned throughput.
A live aircraft position/altitude/speed update received from the ADS-B transponder feed (OpenSky Network), used for ambient traffic awareness.
A recorded schedule deviation on a flight leg, the primary trigger for downstream connection-risk calculations.
A ground stop or holding pattern imposed by ATC or weather, affecting arrival/departure sequencing at an airport.
A defined, governance-gated operational command the recovery planner can propose — deterministic, auditable, and requiring named approval.
Rebooks an at-risk connecting passenger cohort onto an alternate or partner flight and issues EU261 vouchers where applicable. Requires OCC Duty Manager approval.
Opens additional gate/stand hours at an airport and sets a divert threshold above which inbound flights are auto-diverted to a remote stand. Requires Airport Ops Manager approval.
Swaps the aircraft tail number assigned to a flight leg to recover from a mechanical fault or rotation conflict.
Sends proactive passenger notifications when a flight's connection-risk SLA is breached.
An audited record of a proposed or executed action: who proposed it, who approved it, and its resulting side effects.
The global airline trade body that sets interline, cargo, and safety standards airlines and airports operate under.
